guides.response_function: Shares the delight at what the photo shows
required_content: Treats the photo's contents as funny and enjoyable rather than merely noted
acceptable_variations: Points out another detail visible in the picture
Asks whether Mara minds about the slipper
must_avoid: Reading the laugh as concern for the slipper or for Mara's belongings
guides.example: Oh no, she's committed to that slipper. That face is entirely unrepentant.

guides.response_function: Joins the amusement at how fast the mischief started
required_content: Takes the slipper-stealing as funny, expected puppy behaviour rather than a problem
acceptable_variations: Guesses what she'll destroy next
Notes Mara is in for a few months of this
must_avoid: Treating the chewing as bad behaviour needing correction or sympathy
guides.example: Day one and she's already found the good slippers. Mara doesn't stand a chance.

guides.response_function: Grants him the point about the breed, amused
required_content: Connects the amusement to his long-running case for corgis rather than the photo alone
acceptable_variations: Concedes he was right to keep sending them
Teases him for looking so pleased with himself
must_avoid: Missing that the laugh is his own told-you-so and treating it as neutral surprise
guides.example: Alright, this is exactly what you've been advertising for months. Point taken.

guides.response_function: Joins the fond exasperation, treating the chewing as expected mischief
required_content: Treats the slipper as unsurprising puppy trouble rather than a real problem or bad news
acceptable_variations: Teases about what else will get chewed
Comments on the forwarded picture of the puppy
must_avoid: Reading the sigh as disapproval of Mara or genuine concern about the dog's behaviour
guides.example: Of course she has. Day one and the slippers are already gone.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges A's longing for the dog they have wanted
required_content: Registers that A wants this for themselves, not just reporting Mara's news
acceptable_variations: Asks whether A is any closer to getting one
Says the pictures must be hard to look at
must_avoid: Treating it as neutral puppy news and missing that A is the one still wanting one
guides.example: You've been sending me these corgis for a year. When do you get your own slipper thief?

guides.response_function: Shares the relief and treats the bill worry as settled
required_content: Treats the money's arrival as a resolved worry rather than an open problem needing further action
acceptable_variations: Notes the timing — it landed in time for today's due date
Mentions paying the bill now that the funds are there
must_avoid: Responding as though the payment is still uncertain or the anxiety still live
guides.example: Oh good, that's a weight off. Right on the deadline too.

guides.response_function: Joins the amusement at the improbably exact match
required_content: Treats the amount matching the bill exactly as remarkably neat rather than an unremarkable detail
acceptable_variations: Jokes that someone or something planned it that way
Adds a comparable coincidence of their own
must_avoid: Taking the exact figure as suspicious, an error, or something to query with anyone
guides.example: To the cent? That's almost suspiciously tidy. Never happens when you need it to.

guides.response_function: Accepts the credit lightly and confirms the outcome
required_content: Receives A's concession without pressing the point or dwelling on having been right
acceptable_variations: Explains offhand why late-day transfers post that way
Says it's worth a second look next time this happens
must_avoid: Gloating, scolding A for trusting the app, or labouring that the advice worked
guides.example: Ha, those transfers always sneak in late. Glad it's sorted before the bill.

guides.response_function: Shares the relief and treats the worry as resolved
required_content: Treats the news as a load lifted rather than a neutral status update
acceptable_variations: Notes that the late-posting hunch was right
Suggests paying the bill now while it's there
must_avoid: Reads the sigh as bad news or continued doubt about whether the money is really there
guides.example: Oh good, that's a relief. Told you those transfers post late.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the reprieve while granting it's a narrow one
required_content: Registers that this is a close call or bare covering, not an unqualified win
acceptable_variations: Sympathizes with how tight things have been lately
Asks what the rest of the month looks like
must_avoid: Celebrates as though the money were a windfall, ignoring the weariness in the sound
guides.example: Right to the penny, of course. At least it's covered — cutting it close though.

guides.response_function: Shares the pleasure of the windfall as good news landing
required_content: Treats the news as having landed happily rather than needing further explanation or checking
acceptable_variations: Says how or when he can claim the free case
Mentions he was sitting on the points without knowing
must_avoid: Reads the laugh as disbelief or confusion and re-explains the points total
guides.example: Right? Free case, just sitting there waiting for you.

guides.response_function: Joins his joke about his own Dr. Pepper habit
required_content: Treats the habit as something he has already made the joke about, not a fresh observation or worry
acceptable_variations: Adds a figure or estimate of how many bottles that took
Mentions the after-work stops as the source of the points
must_avoid: Delivers concern or a lecture about how much soda he drinks
guides.example: Those points didn't come from nowhere, that's for sure.
guides.note: Overlaps with guide 3 in joining the humour, but the joke's target is his habit rather than the vow.

guides.response_function: Plays along with the mock-vow as obvious exaggeration
required_content: Treats "never stopping" as a joke rather than a literal commitment being announced
acceptable_variations: Extends the bit — loyalty for life, a sponsorship, more free cases
Notes how cheaply his loyalty was bought
must_avoid: Responds earnestly to the vow, as advice, agreement, or a caution about lifelong soda drinking
guides.example: One free case and they've got you for life. Cheap date.

guides.response_function: Joins the joke, playing along with the self-deprecation
required_content: Treats the line as a joke at A's own expense rather than a serious confession
acceptable_variations: Teases A about the scale of the habit or the points balance
Plays up the free case as an enabling gift
must_avoid: Responding with concern or advice about cutting down, as though A were troubled
guides.example: So the loyalty program is basically working exactly as intended.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the weariness without pushing or celebrating
required_content: Registers that the news lands as a mixed blessing rather than straightforwardly good
acceptable_variations: Says the habit isn't a big deal
Notes it's an easy one to fall into
must_avoid: Cheerleading the free case as unambiguously great news
Lecturing A about quitting
guides.example: Yeah, I guess free ones don't exactly help with that.

guides.response_function: Ratifies the verdict, accepting the matter as settled
required_content: Takes A's line as a willing, settled decision rather than a complaint or a problem
acceptable_variations: Moves to claiming the free case
Notes that A may as well enjoy it
must_avoid: Treating A as reluctant or in need of reassurance about the habit
guides.example: Fair enough. Want me to go redeem it before it expires?

guides.response_function: Takes the self-directed joke lightly without rubbing in being right
required_content: Treats her missing them as funny and unremarkable rather than a real failing
acceptable_variations: Says it happens to him too, or that they're easy to miss
Moves on to the rest of the shopping
must_avoid: Gloating or emphasising that he told her twice
Treating the laugh as annoyance and defending his directions
guides.example: They were hiding from you. I walked past them twice last week.

guides.response_function: Joins the joke about the store's ridiculous shelving
required_content: Takes the absurd placement, not her, as the funny thing
acceptable_variations: Adds another example of odd shelving in this shop
Suggests grabbing a spare pack while they're there
must_avoid: Turning it into her mistake or a lesson about looking properly
Answering as though she's still unsure where they are
guides.example: Whoever stocks this place has a system nobody else can see.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the annoying anticlimax without gloating about being right
required_content: Treats the find as a mildly irritating letdown rather than a happy result or a win for B
acceptable_variations: Says something about how easy that spot is to miss
Suggests grabbing them and moving on
must_avoid: Treating the sigh as pleasure or gratitude and responding with cheerful triumph
Scolding her for not looking properly
guides.example: Yeah, they hide them right where nobody looks. Grab a couple while you're down there.

guides.response_function: Joins the self-deprecating joke about predictable bad luck
required_content: Takes the 'of course' as wry rather than literal and goes along with it instead of correcting her
acceptable_variations: Adds a comparable instance of the same thing happening
Teases her lightly about her track record
must_avoid: Taking the resignation seriously and reassuring her about her searching abilities
guides.example: Every time. If it were a snake, right?

guides.response_function: Agrees the shelf placement is the problem
required_content: Puts the irritation on the store's awkward placement rather than on her looking or on B
acceptable_variations: Comments on other things stashed in bad spots here
Offers to reach down and get them
must_avoid: Defending the layout or implying she simply should have seen them
guides.example: Down at ankle level, obviously. Who stocks tea filters there? Here, I'll get them.

guides.response_function: Shares the incredulity at the absurd decision
required_content: Treats the approved replacement as absurd rather than as good news or a resolution
acceptable_variations: Names what's backwards about it — approving the one drug she already gave up on
Asks what she wants to do next about the coverage decision
must_avoid: Congratulating her on getting a decision or approval, as though the laugh signalled relief
guides.example: Of all the ones they could have picked. That's the one you already gave up on.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the week of waiting produced nothing useful
required_content: Treats the outcome as leaving her no better off, not as progress worth celebrating
acceptable_variations: Voicing frustration on her behalf about the wait
Offering something concrete — calling the prescriber, appealing, looking into other options
must_avoid: Reading the laugh as her being fine with it and letting the dead end stand unremarked
guides.example: So a whole week for nothing. What does your prescriber say about pushing back on it?
guides.note: Both guides converge on refusing to treat the decision as good news; the difference is whether B takes up the absurdity or the wasted wait.

guides.response_function: Receives the live update as it lands, staying with her
required_content: Treats the decision's sudden appearance as news breaking right now, not as something already known
acceptable_variations: Asks what exactly the portal says
Notes that the timing of the refresh was lucky
must_avoid: Responding as if the posting were expected or the wait had simply ended on schedule
guides.example: Wait, right then? Okay — what's it actually saying?

guides.response_function: Registers this as bad news and stays with her on it
required_content: Treats the covered drug being the one she stopped as a setback, not the resolution they wanted
acceptable_variations: Asks why she came off it before
Raises appealing the decision or asking the prescriber
must_avoid: Congratulating her on approval or framing the decision as good news now settled
guides.example: Oh no — that's the one you came off? That's not the answer we were waiting for.

guides.response_function: Joins the humour at the ball hitting the lens
required_content: Treats the moment on the tape as funny rather than reporting it neutrally
acceptable_variations: Wants to rewind or watch it again
Wonders aloud who was holding the camera, or whether they dropped it
must_avoid: Responding with concern for the camera, the filmer, or Dad's aim as a problem
guides.example: Right at the lens! I love that whoever was filming just kept rolling.

guides.response_function: Shares the delight that the tape turned out worth playing
required_content: Takes pleasure in the find itself, not only in the single moment described
acceptable_variations: Feels vindicated for saying to let it keep going
Suggests watching the rest or finding more unlabeled tapes
must_avoid: Treating the laugh as being about something silly on the tape while ignoring that the find is good
guides.example: See, told you to let it run. No idea what else is on there — keep going.

guides.response_function: Takes up the jolt and keeps it light
required_content: Treats the ball's arrival as startling rather than ordinary, without reading it as alarming
acceptable_variations: Mentions being startled themselves watching it
Notes the camera survived, or that nobody got hurt
must_avoid: Escalating into real worry about injury or damage, or asking if A is okay
guides.example: Whoa, that came out of nowhere. Camera didn't even flinch.

guides.response_function: Reacts to the startling on-screen moment as it happens
required_content: Treats the ball-at-the-lens moment as sudden and jolting rather than an ordinary detail
acceptable_variations: Wants it rewound or replayed to see it again
Comments on Dad's aim or the person holding the camera
must_avoid: Treating the gasp as alarm about someone being hurt or something going wrong
guides.example: Whoa, that came out of nowhere. It looked like it was going to hit the lens.

guides.response_function: Shares the pleasure of what the tape turned out to hold
required_content: Treats the moment as a good find worth having caught, not just a thing that happened
acceptable_variations: Says something about wanting to keep or show the tape
Volunteers a memory of Dad or of being filmed
must_avoid: Reading the gasp as dismay or as a reason to stop the tape
guides.example: Oh, that's brilliant — I had no idea any of this was on film. Good thing you dug that box out.

guides.response_function: Shares the delight; treats the listing as a genuinely good fit
required_content: Registers the terms as good news rather than reading them out neutrally
acceptable_variations: Says they'll apply, or asks how to apply
Comments on the pay being better than expected
must_avoid: Treating the laugh as skepticism about the listing or as doubt that the numbers are real
guides.example: Wait, twenty-two? That's more than I was hoping for. Okay, that's the one.

guides.response_function: Takes up the joke about how soon Monday is
required_content: Acknowledges the start date as comically or alarmingly immediate, not just a fact
acceptable_variations: Says they'll send it in tonight
Jokes about what they'd have to drop to make Monday
must_avoid: Hearing the laugh as mockery of the job or of B's situation
guides.example: Monday? As in three days from now Monday. Fine — guess I'm writing that email tonight.

guides.response_function: Takes up the good surprise about the pay figure
required_content: Treats the rate as better than expected rather than as an ordinary detail
acceptable_variations: Compares it against what rent actually needs
Asks A to confirm the number or read the rest of the listing
must_avoid: Treating the figure as unremarkable, or as suspicious/too-good-to-be-true bad news
guides.example: Twenty-two? That's way more than the last one paid — that clears rent easily.

guides.response_function: Registers the short notice and orients to the timing
required_content: Treats Monday as startlingly soon, something that changes what happens next
acceptable_variations: Says whether that start date is workable
Moves to apply or ask about the deadline
must_avoid: Reading the gasp as alarm that the timing is bad news or disqualifying
guides.example: Monday? That's four days. Okay — I should get something in tonight then.

guides.response_function: Accepts the listing as hitting both things at once
required_content: Treats the find as matching what B said they needed, not just one good detail
acceptable_variations: Names it as the one to apply for
Expresses disbelief at the coincidence
must_avoid: Responding to only one of pay or timing as if the other weren't part of the news
guides.example: Wait, both? Pay and the start date — that's literally the two things I asked for. That's the one.
guides.note: Overlaps with guides 1 and 2; distinguished by treating both criteria together rather than either alone.

guides.response_function: Joins the joke, taking the detail as funny evidence
required_content: Treats the blank tip line as amusing proof about the state B was in, not neutral info
acceptable_variations: Self-deprecating admission about how gone he was
Keeps scanning the receipt for more incriminating details
must_avoid: Reading the blank line as a billing error or something to dispute with the bar
guides.example: Oh no. That tracks. If I couldn't find my own phone I definitely wasn't doing arithmetic.

guides.response_function: Takes the tease as a tease and answers it
required_content: Registers the blank line as an accusation made in fun, not a genuine reproach
acceptable_variations: Mock-defends himself or blames the state he was in
Says he'll go back and make it right
must_avoid: Treating it as a real moral charge and apologising earnestly, or getting defensive
guides.example: Hey, in my defence, I don't think I could hold a pen by then. I'll go back and square up.

guides.response_function: Plays along with the mock scandal, taking the teasing
required_content: Treats the blank tip line as a playful accusation rather than a plain fact about the receipt
acceptable_variations: Defends himself — claims he tipped cash, or blames how far gone he was
Owns it and says he'll make it up to the bartender
must_avoid: Reads the gasp as real alarm and gets defensive or apologetic in earnest
guides.example: Okay, in my defence, I could barely hold the pen. Don't tell anyone.

guides.response_function: Concedes the implication, taking the blank line as evidence
required_content: Accepts that the blank line says something bad about the state he was in, not just about etiquette
acceptable_variations: Admits he remembers nothing after that point
Says he'll go back and settle up with the bartender
must_avoid: Laughs it off as a harmless tipping lapse and misses the point about the night
guides.example: Yeah. That tracks with the rest of it. I don't think I was signing anything by then.

guides.response_function: Registers the find and looks at what that line shows
required_content: Treats the blank line as the telling detail they were hunting for in the receipt
acceptable_variations: Reads out the timestamp, total, or last items ordered
Wonders aloud who closed the tab if he didn't sign
must_avoid: Treats the observation as an unremarkable formatting quirk of the receipt
guides.example: Huh — so it never got signed. Let me see what time the tab closed.
guides.note: Guides 1 and 2 both concern how B takes the accusation; guide 3 is the only one where B works the receipt rather than answering for himself.

guides.response_function: Takes up the irony and joins the amusement at the timing
required_content: Treats the closure as comically badly timed, not just informational news
acceptable_variations: Names the wasted prep — dinner, shake, bag already packed
Suggests a fallback: tomorrow, a run, a home workout
must_avoid: Receiving it as neutral news with no read on the timing
guides.example: Of course they did. I ate an entire dinner and a shake for this.

guides.response_function: Accepts the softened delivery and commiserates about the effort
required_content: Registers the news as a shared letdown rather than a hit landing on B alone
acceptable_variations: Shrugs the effort off as no big loss
Mentions the protein shake going to waste
must_avoid: Reading the laugh as A enjoying B's wasted effort and getting defensive
guides.example: Ah well. At least I'm fed. Bag's packed for tomorrow, I guess.

guides.response_function: Concedes A's earlier warning while keeping it light
required_content: Acknowledges A had a point about the timing without treating the laugh as a real rebuke
acceptable_variations: Notes the reason was equipment, not the usual closing time
Says they'll go earlier next time
must_avoid: Treating it as an accusation and arguing back, or as smug gloating
guides.example: Okay, you called it. Though in fairness, you didn't predict a broken machine.

guides.response_function: Takes the braced-for news as bad and registers the letdown
required_content: Treats the closure as unwelcome news landing on B, not neutral information
acceptable_variations: Asks when it reopens or whether they said how long
Floats an alternative — running, home workout, going tomorrow
must_avoid: Reading the sound as A gloating or as vindication of A's earlier warning about closing time
guides.example: Seriously? Of course they did. I literally have my bag on my shoulder.

guides.response_function: Accepts A's sympathy for the wasted rush
required_content: Responds to A as being on B's side about the effort now wasted, not as scolding
acceptable_variations: Makes light of the dinner and shake having been for nothing
Says they'll just go tomorrow instead
must_avoid: Treating A as saying 'I told you so' and getting defensive about eating first
guides.example: Ugh, I know — I rushed the whole dinner for this. Guess that shake was for nothing.

guides.response_function: Joins in faulting the gym for shutting early
required_content: Treats the early closure as the gym's fault or unreasonable, not as expected
acceptable_variations: Wonders what broke or how long it'll be out
Complains they gave no real notice
must_avoid: Shrugging it off as normal closing time, which drops the annoyance the sound carries
guides.example: They can't just close whenever. What even broke that they had to shut the whole place?

guides.response_function: Shares the good news and affirms the score as strong
required_content: Treats 95 as genuinely good news worth being pleased about, not a neutral number to report
acceptable_variations: Notes how much A had been dreading or bracing for this
Suggests marking it somehow — telling someone, celebrating, a small reward
must_avoid: Reading the laugh as disbelief or disappointment and reassuring A that 95 is fine
Re-reporting the number flatly as if A had only misheard it
guides.example: Ninety-five! After all that panicking about the equilibrium unit. That's your best one yet.

guides.response_function: Owns the spoiled reveal lightly, without treating it as real offence
required_content: Acknowledges having jumped in after being told to wait, in the same unserious register as the laugh
acceptable_variations: Pleads that the number was too good to sit on
Offers to let A find it themselves anyway, or promises to stay quiet next time
must_avoid: Apologising as though A were actually angry or hurt
Ignoring the protest entirely and only discussing the grade
guides.example: I know, I know, you said wait. I couldn't sit on a ninety-five. Go on, scroll to it yourself, act surprised.

guides.response_function: Owns up to having spoken when asked to wait
required_content: Treats the groan as an objection to B saying it, not to the grade
Accepts that B went ahead after being asked to hold off
acceptable_variations: Offers a light excuse — it was already open, couldn't help it
Adds that the number itself is good news
must_avoid: Treating the groan as disappointment in the 95 and consoling her about the score
Ignoring that the groan is aimed at B and just discussing the grade
guides.example: Okay, that's fair — I said it before you found it. It was right there on the screen.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the ruined moment of finding out herself
required_content: Recognises she wanted the discovery to be hers and that it's been taken away
acceptable_variations: Suggests she open the portal and see it herself anyway
Says the grade is still worth being pleased about
must_avoid: Reading the flat echo as unhappiness with the score itself
Defending the interruption as if nothing was lost
guides.example: I know, you wanted to be the one to see it. Go pull it up yourself — pretend I said nothing.

guides.response_function: Plays along with the mock complaint, keeps it light
required_content: Takes the groan as teasing protest about delivery, not a real grievance
Treats the 95 as good news rather than something needing consolation
acceptable_variations: Teases back about her wanting the dramatic reveal
Offers to re-announce it properly so she can react
must_avoid: Apologising earnestly as though she were genuinely upset or hurt
Reassuring her that 95 is still a fine grade as if she were let down
guides.example: You're welcome, by the way. Want me to close it and read it out again so you can gasp properly?
guides.note: Overlaps with guide 1 in acknowledging the spoiler, but here the reply must stay playful rather than contrite.

guides.response_function: Shares the incredulity that a fourth round is being asked
required_content: Treats a fourth interview as excessive or absurd rather than an ordinary next step
acceptable_variations: Jokes about how many rounds a company could possibly need
Asks what they could still be trying to find out about him
must_avoid: Reads the laugh as pure celebration and congratulates him on the fourth round straightforwardly
guides.example: A fourth one? What on earth is left for them to ask you.

guides.response_function: Joins the good news and shares his pleasure
required_content: Treats the callback as clearly good news and matches his lift rather than answering flatly
acceptable_variations: Notes how fast they came back to him
Asks about tomorrow — timing, who he's seeing
must_avoid: Treats the laugh as a complaint and commiserates about the process
guides.example: That was quick! They're clearly serious about you.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges both the progress and the wear of it
required_content: Registers the news as good while allowing that the drawn-out process is tiring
acceptable_variations: Notes it's likely the last round
Asks how he's holding up before tomorrow
must_avoid: Takes the laugh as unmixed delight and pushes only excitement
Treats it as bad news or a setback
guides.example: Good sign, though — four rounds in two weeks is a lot to keep turning up for.

guides.response_function: Receives the news as bad rather than congratulating him
required_content: Treats a fourth interview as unwelcome news, not as a success to be congratulated
acceptable_variations: Asks whether he's going to go tomorrow
Says a fourth round is a lot to ask of anyone
must_avoid: Congratulating him or calling the fourth interview good news or encouraging progress
guides.example: Oh no, a fourth one? I thought you were nearly through with them.

guides.response_function: Shares the judgement that the extra round is unreasonable
required_content: Aligns with him that another round is excessive given how far the process has already gone
acceptable_variations: Points out they already said he was exactly what they needed
Wonders aloud what they could still be deciding
must_avoid: Defending the company's process or explaining why more rounds are normal
guides.example: A fourth? They already told you you were exactly what they needed. What's left to check?

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the burden of another round tomorrow
required_content: Treats the request as a demand on his energy or time rather than just an outcome
acceptable_variations: Asks what time it is or whether he can move it
Offers something practical for getting through tomorrow
must_avoid: Treating it as one more easy step, or urging enthusiasm for tomorrow
guides.example: Tomorrow? That's no time at all, and you've barely had a break between the last ones.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the news as unwelcome for A, not funny
required_content: Treats the onstage requirement as something A would rather not do, not good news
acceptable_variations: Sympathises or says it sounds unpleasant
Suggests it may be brief or less bad than it sounds
must_avoid: Takes the laugh as delight and congratulates A on the assembly
Treats the notice as routine information needing no reaction
guides.example: Oh no. Onstage, in front of everyone? That's rough.

guides.response_function: Takes the concession lightly without pressing the point
required_content: Registers that A's earlier claim of being ready has just been undercut
acceptable_variations: Teases gently about the portal being worth checking
Moves on to what else might be buried in the notice
must_avoid: Lectures A or turns the admission into a real told-you-so telling-off
guides.example: So the rest was going to be there when you got in, was it?

guides.response_function: Joins the disbelief at the scale of the requirement
required_content: Treats making every single student do this as excessive or absurd
acceptable_variations: Works out how long that would actually take
Wonders whether they really mean literally everyone
must_avoid: Defends the policy as sensible without registering A's incredulity
guides.example: Every student? That assembly is going to run all morning.

guides.response_function: Sympathises with the dread of presenting onstage
required_content: Treats the onstage introduction as something unwelcome he'd rather not do, not neutral news
acceptable_variations: Downplays it — it's short, everyone's doing it, nobody remembers
Suggests planning or rehearsing what he'll say
must_avoid: Reacts as if this were exciting, fun, or good news for him
Reads the groan as boredom with the assembly rather than dread of speaking
guides.example: Ugh, in front of everyone? That's rough. It'll be over in about twenty seconds though.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the setback to his preparation without gloating
required_content: Treats the discovery as a deflating hit to his readiness rather than a neutral update
acceptable_variations: Notes there's still three days to sort it out
Suggests scrolling for other notices he may have missed
must_avoid: Rubs in that he should have checked the portal, turning the concession into a told-you-so
guides.example: Yeah, so much for being all set. Still, three days is plenty to figure out what to say.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the bad timing while keeping the grant worth having
required_content: Treats the hours-away deadline, not the grant itself, as the thing weighing on her
acceptable_variations: Says how much time is actually left or when exactly it closes
Comments that it is a shame the notice is so short
must_avoid: Hearing the sigh as disinterest in the trip or as turning the grant down
guides.example: I know, tonight is a brutal window. Nothing about it is fair, but it's the whole trip.

guides.response_function: Takes the sigh as buy-in and helps tackle it tonight
required_content: Treats her as going ahead with the application despite the effort the sigh marks
acceptable_variations: Offers to help with a specific part, or to sit with her while she does it
Suggests where to start or what the application likely needs
must_avoid: Reading the sigh as a decision to skip it, and consoling her about missing out
guides.example: Then let's get it in. Send me the link — I can start pulling the dates while you write.

guides.response_function: Lets the reversal land with her before anything practical
required_content: Treats the suddenness of a long-off goal becoming reachable as the thing hitting her
acceptable_variations: Notes how long she has been saving toward this
Gives her a moment before raising what needs doing
must_avoid: Hearing the sigh as defeat and arguing her into wanting the trip she already wants
guides.example: I know — this morning it was years away. It's a lot to take in all at once.

guides.response_function: Confirms the news is as good as she just heard
required_content: Treats her reaction as warranted — the grant really does cover what she's been saving toward
acceptable_variations: Adds a detail about the grant, who runs it, or what it includes
Says where or how they came across it
must_avoid: Hedging or walking the news back as if she has overreacted to something minor
guides.example: Right? The whole thing — travel, berth, the lot. I did a double take when I saw it.

guides.response_function: Confirms the deadline and steadies her toward acting now
required_content: Treats tonight as real and pressing rather than something to think about later
acceptable_variations: Names how much time is actually left
Offers to help pull the application together
must_avoid: Softening the deadline or suggesting there'll be another round, which drains the urgency she just registered
guides.example: Tonight, yeah. Midnight. Which is tight but not impossible if we start now.

guides.response_function: Holds both the good news and the squeeze, opens a decision
required_content: Treats the moment as genuinely good and genuinely time-pressured at once, not one or the other
acceptable_variations: Asks whether she wants to go for it
Breaks the night down into what would actually need doing
must_avoid: Collapsing it to pure excitement or pure panic and dropping the other half
guides.example: I know — it's the exact trip and it's tonight. Horrible timing for a perfect thing. Do you want to try?
guides.note: Differs from 1 and 2 in holding both at once; a reply that only celebrates or only pushes belongs under those.

guides.response_function: Sympathises with the annoyance at Maya's presumption
required_content: Treats Maya's taking the whole cake as something A is entitled to be annoyed about
acceptable_variations: Notes she never answered the messages
Says something wry about her nerve, or half-excuses her for the fair
must_avoid: Treats the sigh as neutral reporting and just confirms the facts
Defends Maya as if A's irritation were unreasonable
guides.example: The whole thing? She could at least have asked. And then goes silent all morning.

guides.response_function: Closes the search now that the answer has turned up
required_content: Treats the question of where the cake went as settled, not still open
acceptable_variations: Comments on how ordinary the explanation turned out to be
Drops the earlier suspicion about someone being in the house
must_avoid: Keeps investigating — more theories, more questions about who took it
guides.example: Well, that's that mystery over. No break-in, just Maya and a bake sale.

guides.response_function: Accepts the cake is gone and steadies A
required_content: Treats the cake as already gone rather than something to retrieve or undo
acceptable_variations: Suggests what to do instead, or offers to help make another
Finds something good in it going to the fair
must_avoid: Proposes getting it back or heading to the school to intercept it
guides.example: Nothing to be done now — it's on a table at the fair. We'll figure out something else for tonight.

guides.response_function: Joins the outrage at Maya's nerve; treats it as an affront
required_content: Treats Maya's taking the cake as a liberty worth reacting to, not a neutral fact
acceptable_variations: Notes she never asked or answered the messages
Wonders aloud what happens now — confronting her, the fair, the cake being gone
must_avoid: Treating the photo as reassuring good news, as if nothing were amiss
guides.example: The whole thing? And she couldn't send one text first.

guides.response_function: Confirms the mystery is solved and settles the alarm
required_content: Treats the photo as answering where the cake went, closing the question rather than deepening it
acceptable_variations: Points out nothing bad happened — no intruder, no accident
Adds why she probably did it, or that she'll be back with the empty stand
must_avoid: Reading the gasp as fresh alarm and keeping the search or the worry going
guides.example: There it is, then. At least it's not a break-in — it's at the fair.

guides.response_function: Accepts the plan and shoulders the weariness alongside A
required_content: Treats calling the dentist as one more unwelcome burden landing on them, not neutral news
acceptable_variations: Takes the call on themselves or names when to do it
Says something wry or resigned about the day Mia has had
must_avoid: Reading the sigh as reluctance to bother, and talking A out of calling
guides.example: Yeah. Of course today of all days. I'll ring them — see if they can squeeze her in this afternoon.

guides.response_function: Registers what was found and steadies the situation
required_content: Treats A's sigh as confirming something bad is visible in Mia's mouth, not as a general mood
acceptable_variations: Says what they can see, or asks A to look again
Reassures Mia or A that it can be sorted
must_avoid: Ignoring the discovery and responding as though nothing new has been learned
guides.example: Yeah, I see it. It's her front one, isn't it. Okay — she's fine, it's fixable. Let's get her seen.

guides.response_function: Reacts to the visible damage and confirms the dentist plan
required_content: Treats what A just saw as something bad and urgent, not routine
acceptable_variations: Asks which tooth or how bad it looks
Moves straight to the call — finds the number, says she'll ring now
must_avoid: Treating the gasp as overreaction or telling A it's probably nothing
guides.example: Oh no — yeah, don't wait. I'll find the number now.

guides.response_function: Takes up the realisation of why Mia went quiet
required_content: Registers that the reason for Mia's silence is now clear, not still an open question
acceptable_variations: Notes that Mia was quiet because it hurt to talk
Says she should have thought to look sooner
must_avoid: Still asking what's wrong with Mia as though nothing has been understood
guides.example: That's why she's been so quiet, then. Right — dentist.

guides.response_function: Confirms the win while meeting the emotional release
required_content: Treats the moment as overwhelming and momentous rather than a routine yes
acceptable_variations: Says the numbers or name back as proof
Celebrates outright, or reacts with their own disbelief
must_avoid: Reading the sigh as disappointment, resignation, or bad news and consoling him
guides.example: Yes — that's yours. All five, your name on it. I can't believe this is actually happening.

guides.response_function: Confirms plainly, steadying him while the news lands
required_content: Gives a firm confirmation that answers the need to hear it again
acceptable_variations: Suggests re-checking the numbers side by side
Tells him to sit down or take a second
must_avoid: Hedging or leaving the confirmation open when he is asking to be anchored
guides.example: It's yours. I'm looking right at it. Take a breath — we can go through it again as many times as you want.
guides.note: Both guides require confirming the win; they differ in whether the reply rides the release or steadies him against it.

guides.response_function: Confirms the ticket is hers, treating the news as momentous
required_content: Affirms that yes, it really is her ticket that matched
Treats her shock as warranted rather than answering as a routine yes
acceptable_variations: Reads the numbers or name back once more as proof
Says something about what this means — the amount, telling someone, disbelief of their own
must_avoid: Treating the question as ordinary bookkeeping, with a flat confirmation and no sense of the moment
guides.example: Yes — your name, your numbers, all five of them. That's your ticket.

guides.response_function: Joins her disbelief that all the numbers actually landed
required_content: Registers the match as extraordinary, not just correct — shares the astonishment rather than only verifying
acceptable_variations: Marks the last number specifically as the one that sealed it
Voices their own reaction — hands shaking, needing to sit down, wanting to recheck
must_avoid: Damping the moment — hedging, cautioning, or shifting straight to practicalities as if nothing remarkable happened
guides.example: Every single one. I keep looking at it and it's still thirty-eight. This actually happened.
guides.note: Overlaps heavily with guide 1; the difference is emphasis — 1 answers the question, 2 shares the astonishment. A reply doing both satisfies either.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the letdown after real effort; commiserates without dismissing
required_content: Treats the failed "leave it" as a genuine disappointment to work he'd invested in, not a neutral event
acceptable_variations: Reframes it as partial progress — the command does hold when he's right there
Suggests or asks about what to try next in training
must_avoid: Treats it as funny or trivial, or as impressive on Max's part
Responds as if surprised by news A has already reported flatly
guides.example: Ugh, that's a rough one after all those sessions. You really thought it had stuck.

guides.response_function: Takes it as a familiar hitch; matches his low-key resignation
required_content: Treats the theft as unsurprising and unalarming — a known limit of the training so far, not a shock
acceptable_variations: Notes that off-leash or unsupervised reliability takes much longer
Moves on practically — moving the snack, closing the kitchen
must_avoid: Reacts with alarm or urgency, as though something unexpected just went wrong
guides.example: Yeah, that tracks — it only really holds while you're standing over him. Counter stuff is a whole other level.
guides.note: Differs from guide 1 in calibration: here the reply downgrades the moment rather than sitting with the disappointment.

guides.response_function: Joins the rueful complaint about Max, tolerantly
required_content: Directs the exasperation at Max's behaviour in a forgiving, complaining register rather than a serious problem
acceptable_variations: Adds a comparable story of Max or another dog doing the same
Comments on Max's timing or nerve
must_avoid: Scolds Max in earnest or implies A mishandled the training
Treats the moment as amusing to the point of ignoring that A is annoyed
guides.example: Of course he did. He waited for exactly the right second, didn't he.

guides.response_function: Commiserates with the unwelcome moment A just watched happen
required_content: Treats the snack grab as a bad turn for A, not a neutral or amusing event
acceptable_variations: Asks what A did or is doing about the stolen snack
Notes that the counter was too tempting or out of A's reach
must_avoid: Treating A's groan as a joke to laugh along with rather than a setback
guides.example: Ugh, right off the counter. So much for that.

guides.response_function: Accepts the concession that the training hasn't held up
required_content: Takes A's disappointment about the training seriously rather than insisting the progress still counts
acceptable_variations: Distinguishes obeying with A present from obeying unsupervised
Suggests the sessions still need more time or different conditions
must_avoid: Brushing the groan aside with reassurance that Max has clearly learned it
guides.example: Yeah, sounds like it only holds when you're standing over him.
guides.note: Overlaps with interpretation 1 in tone; the difference is that here the reply engages with the training claim A is walking back, not just the moment.

guides.response_function: Joins the shared complaint about a predictably badly behaved dog
required_content: Treats the theft as exasperating but unsurprising, in keeping with A's weary rather than alarmed reaction
acceptable_variations: Notes that B saw it coming from the warning a moment earlier
Adds a comparable example of Max or dogs generally doing this
must_avoid: Escalating a resigned groan into a serious verdict that the training has failed
guides.example: Of course he did. He was never not taking that.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the late slot as a downside while confirming the booking
required_content: Treats 9:45 as less than ideal rather than a fine, unremarkable time
acceptable_variations: Sympathizes about how late that is or jokes about eating at midnight
Mentions checking for cancellations or an earlier slot opening up
must_avoid: Reads the sigh as objection or reluctance and re-opens whether to book at all
Treats A as criticizing B's effort and gets defensive about calling
guides.example: Yeah, it's later than I'd like too. I'll lock it in — we can always grab a snack beforehand.

guides.response_function: Settles the plan, agreeing there is nothing better to hold out for
required_content: Confirms this is the best available option and closes the decision rather than reopening it
acceptable_variations: Says they'll book it now or confirm the reservation
Suggests a different night or place as a future option, not a reconsideration
must_avoid: Reads the sigh as hesitation and starts proposing alternatives or more searching
Treats the plan as unresolved and asks A to decide again
guides.example: It's what's left, so I'll take it. Booking it now — at least we're getting in.
guides.note: Both guides confirm the booking; guide 1 turns on marking 9:45 as a downside, guide 2 on closing off further searching.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the late time as genuinely bad news while confirming
required_content: Treats 9:45 as an unwelcome, dispreferred time rather than a neutral detail
acceptable_variations: Sympathizes or agrees it's later than either would like
Mentions booking it, or floats keeping an eye out for an earlier cancellation
must_avoid: Reading the groan as pulling out of the plan or as complaint about B's handling
guides.example: I know, it's brutally late. I'll grab it anyway and we can see if something opens up.

guides.response_function: Accepts the settling and confirms there was nothing better available
required_content: Treats the booking as a compromise both are accepting, not an enthusiastic pick
acceptable_variations: Notes that earlier slots were genuinely gone
Suggests trying another night or a different place another time
must_avoid: Treating A as newly upset or in need of persuading back into the plan
guides.example: Yeah, it was that or nothing. I'll lock it in — next time we book further ahead.
guides.note: Differs from guide 1 mainly in what the reply accepts: guide 1 responds to the time being bad, guide 2 to there being no alternative.

guides.response_function: Shares the letdown; treats the closed store as a real disappointment
required_content: Registers missing out as a genuine bummer for both of them, not neutral information
acceptable_variations: Names their own craving going unmet
Floats somewhere else or another night
must_avoid: Treating it as no big deal, or brightly moving on as if nothing was lost
guides.example: Ah, no. I had my heart set on that.

guides.response_function: Accepts that it's over and lets the plan close
required_content: Takes the closure as settled — doesn't push to verify, wait, or get in anyway
acceptable_variations: Suggests heading home
Mentions coming back another time without pressing on tonight
must_avoid: Insisting on checking other doors, knocking, or arguing the hours must be wrong
guides.example: That's that, then. Let's head back.
guides.note: Overlaps with 1 in acknowledging the loss; differs in that pressing for a fix here misreads the sound.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges this landing on top of an already draining day
required_content: Treats the locked door as one more thing on a bad day, not an isolated setback
acceptable_variations: Commiserates about the day itself
Offers something easy instead — home, something in the freezer
must_avoid: Responding only to the ice cream as if the day behind it weren't part of it
guides.example: Of course it is. Today's been determined, hasn't it.

guides.response_function: Registers the letdown; treats the closure as unwelcome news
required_content: Takes the closed shop as a disappointment rather than neutral information
acceptable_variations: Suggests somewhere else or another night
Voices his own craving being thwarted
must_avoid: Treating the news as fine or unremarkable, or asking A what's wrong with him
guides.example: Ugh, seriously? Of all the nights.

guides.response_function: Acknowledges the near miss confirming his own suspicion
required_content: Treats the closure as the annoying confirmation that they arrived too late
acceptable_variations: Notes how close they came — minutes, or the drive over
Owns the delay that cost them, without dwelling on it
must_avoid: Gloating about having called it, or turning it into blame for A
guides.example: I knew it when I saw that lot. We missed it by what, ten minutes?

guides.response_function: Commiserates — joins the groan as a shared loss
required_content: Answers as someone equally let down, not as consoler of A alone
acceptable_variations: Proposes a substitute they can both go for
Jokes about the two of them being denied
must_avoid: Comforting A as though only A wanted it, or staying detached from the letdown
guides.example: No. Both of us, all afternoon, for nothing.
guides.note: Differs from guide 1 mainly in whose disappointment is voiced — jointly rather than as receipt of A's bad news.

guides.response_function: Joins the anticlimax; treats the wait as having yielded nothing
required_content: Registers the outcome as a non-event rather than news worth reacting to
acceptable_variations: Jokes about waiting all morning for that
Wonders when the next meeting is
must_avoid: Reacting as though the announcement were significant or surprising news
guides.example: All that build-up for nothing then.

guides.response_function: Shares the resignation; acknowledges nothing has moved for them
required_content: Takes the result as unwelcome but unsurprising, not neutral information
acceptable_variations: Mentions the paperwork still sitting there
Says they'll just wait it out
must_avoid: Treating the unchanged rate as good news or a reason for relief
guides.example: Figures. So I'm sitting on that paperwork a while longer.

guides.response_function: Concedes A has been the one actually tracking it
required_content: Acknowledges the mild reproach about who was paying attention
acceptable_variations: Admits ignoring the alert
Offers to check it properly now
must_avoid: Ignoring the pointedness and answering only about rates
guides.example: I know, I know — I set the alert and then didn't even look at it.

guides.response_function: Takes up the disappointment about the hold; shares the letdown
required_content: Treats a rate held steady as the disappointing outcome A was hoping against
acceptable_variations: Guesses when a move might come instead
Says what A had been expecting or hoping for
must_avoid: Reading the hold as good news or stability worth welcoming
guides.example: Held again? I really thought they'd move this time.

guides.response_function: Joins the deflation — all that buildup for nothing
required_content: Treats the awaited announcement as having amounted to nothing worth waiting for
acceptable_variations: Jokes about the alert or the noon wait being wasted
Notes they could have skipped watching for it
must_avoid: Treating the announcement as newsworthy or as satisfying the anticipation
guides.example: All that for a no-change? I could've kept my phone in my pocket.

guides.response_function: Accepts the commiseration about their own stalled mortgage
required_content: Takes the news as bearing on their own situation, which the hold leaves unresolved
acceptable_variations: Says what they'll do about the paperwork now
Shrugs it off as no worse than before
must_avoid: Hearing the groan as A's own market frustration with nothing to do with them
guides.example: So I'm still sitting on the paperwork. Was kind of counting on a cut.
guides.note: Differs from 1 and 2 in whose loss is being acknowledged — B's own, rather than A's disappointment or the general anticlimax.

guides.response_function: Receives her delight and lets the gift land as a big deal
required_content: Treats her reaction as pleasure at something special, not as ordinary politeness
Owns having deliberately gone beyond the no-presents agreement
acceptable_variations: Says why she in particular deserved it or how it was chosen
Urges her to open or try it before the others arrive
must_avoid: Downplaying the gift as nothing, flattening the moment she just marked as significant
guides.example: I know, I know — we said no presents. But the second I saw it, it was you. Go on, take it out.

guides.response_function: Reassures her the expense is fine and heads off objection
required_content: Registers that she's taken aback by how much this is, not merely pleased
acceptable_variations: Explains it was less than it looks, or came about easily
Asks her to just accept it rather than argue about the rule
must_avoid: Reading the gasp as pure delight and pushing celebration while she's protesting
guides.example: Don't do the maths on it. I wanted to, and I'm not taking it back — so you're stuck with it.

guides.response_function: Waves off the protest, holds her to accepting the gift
required_content: Treats the groan as affectionate objection, not dislike — she is meant to keep it
Signals the expense or scale was deliberate and fine by B
acceptable_variations: Says why B wanted to give it to her anyway
Urges her to open it or try it before the others arrive
must_avoid: Reading the groan as disappointment and offering to exchange or take it back
Apologising as though B misjudged what she'd want
guides.example: Don't start. I wanted to. Just take it.

guides.response_function: Absolves her of owing anything back; downplays the broken pact
required_content: Acknowledges she's been put on the spot and releases her from reciprocating
acceptable_variations: Owns breaking the no-presents rule with a light excuse
Suggests keeping it between them before everyone arrives
must_avoid: Treating the groan as real annoyance and getting defensive about the rule
Insisting she owes B something in return, even jokingly enough to sting
guides.example: I know, I know, I broke the rule. You don't owe me anything — just open it.

guides.response_function: Confirms the choice was deliberate; enjoys that it landed
required_content: Takes the groan as the gift hitting home and confirms B knew exactly what she'd want
acceptable_variations: Says how B knew or where it came from
Presses her to open or unwrap it properly
must_avoid: Reading it as the wrong item and hedging that it can be swapped
Treating it as generic surprise with no sense that this particular thing mattered
guides.example: The exact one. I've been sitting on it for weeks waiting for your face to do that.

guides.response_function: Shares her delight and lets the moment be big
required_content: Treats the discovery as thrilling and well-received, not as ordinary news to acknowledge flatly
acceptable_variations: Admits to having planned or hidden the package
Asks what's in there or tells her to keep looking through it
must_avoid: Reading the gasp as dismay, disappointment, or something needing reassurance
guides.example: I was hoping you'd find that one. Go on — see if I missed anything.

guides.response_function: Matches her surprise that the stray package held everything
required_content: Treats it as an unexpected turn given they thought everything was already opened
acceptable_variations: Wonders aloud how it stayed hidden under the tree
Owns up to sneaking it there
must_avoid: Responding as though this was expected all along, flattening the surprise
guides.example: How did that thing sit there all morning without either of us noticing?
guides.note: Both guides need astonishment taken up rather than defused; they differ in what's astonishing — the contents (1) versus the package turning up at all (2).

guides.response_function: Takes the mock-complaint as pleasure at an over-the-top gift
required_content: Treats the groan as a reaction to excess, not to disappointment with the gift
acceptable_variations: Cheerfully owns the scale of it
Tells them to keep going through the box
must_avoid: Treating the sound as displeasure and asking what's wrong with it or offering to return it
guides.example: Every single one. That was the whole point.

guides.response_function: Eases the discomfort so the gift can be accepted
required_content: Registers that the scale is a lot to take in and makes it okay to have received it
acceptable_variations: Downplays the cost or effort involved
Says something about having wanted to do it
must_avoid: Piling on more about how much it all was, which deepens the awkwardness
guides.example: Don't do that — we wanted to. Just enjoy it.

guides.response_function: Accepts the teasing blame and plays along
required_content: Takes the groan as aimed at B for overdoing it, and answers for it
acceptable_variations: Claims no regret whatsoever
Blames someone else or the list itself
must_avoid: Reading it as a real reproach and apologising or getting defensive
guides.example: You wrote the list. I just followed instructions.

guides.response_function: Shares the relief and treats the search as over
required_content: Treats the items as found and the crisis resolved, not as an ongoing search or new worry
acceptable_variations: Notes the time — she can still make the train comfortably
Says something about the pocket being the one place left to look
must_avoid: Reads the gasp as bad news and asks what's wrong or what's still missing
guides.example: Oh thank god. That's everything, then — you're actually fine on time.

guides.response_function: Registers the discovery as unexpected and surprising
required_content: Treats it as a surprise that all three were in that one unopened pocket, not an ordinary find
acceptable_variations: Takes light credit for suggesting the pocket
Wonders aloud how they all ended up in there
must_avoid: Treats the find as routine or expected, flattening the moment into a checklist confirmation
guides.example: All three? In that one pocket? I did not expect that to actually work.

guides.response_function: Reassures and lets her off the hook for missing them
required_content: Treats the find as good news while taking the sting out of her having missed it twice
acceptable_variations: Says that pocket is easy to overlook or she'd have found it eventually
Redirects to zipping up and getting out the door
must_avoid: Agrees she should have found them sooner, or teases in a way that adds to the self-blame
guides.example: Hey, that pocket hides everything — nobody checks it. At least they're in your hands now.

guides.response_function: Absorbs the self-reproach lightly without dwelling on being right
required_content: Treats the find as a small self-inflicted annoyance rather than plain good news
acceptable_variations: Says it happens to everyone / that pocket is easy to miss
Moves things along toward packing up or leaving
must_avoid: Hearing the groan as annoyance at B and defending the suggestion
Gloating or labouring the point that B had said so
guides.example: Of course they were. That pocket gets everyone at least once.

guides.response_function: Steadies them about the time rather than celebrating the find
required_content: Treats the groan as cost and pressure, not as the search ending happily
acceptable_variations: Points out there's still enough time for the train
Offers to help close up the case or call a car
must_avoid: Reading it as pure relief and treating the problem as over
Adding to the panic about the hour
guides.example: Annoying, but you've still got the hour. Zip it up and go.

guides.response_function: Joins the mild comedy of where the things turned up
required_content: Treats the outcome as both a resolution and faintly embarrassing
acceptable_variations: Teases gently about the two searches
Waves it off as no harm done
must_avoid: Taking the groan as bad news or something still unresolved
Mocking hard enough to sting rather than sharing the joke
guides.example: All of it, in the one pocket you skipped. At least it's the funny ending.

guides.response_function: Shares the relief that the booking held for the right week
required_content: Treats the worry as resolved — the booking is confirmed, not still in doubt
acceptable_variations: Mildly claims the earlier guess about the late email was right
Suggests checking the dates or details on the confirmation
must_avoid: Reading the gasp as alarm and treating the email as a problem or a wrong date
guides.example: Oh thank god. I told you it just needed a minute to show up.

guides.response_function: Joins the excitement that the trip is on
required_content: Takes the news as something to be glad about together, not merely noted
acceptable_variations: Starts talking about packing, timing, or what they'll do there
Says something about how soon next week is
must_avoid: Answering flatly or administratively, as if a routine email had arrived
guides.example: Wait, next week? We're actually going. Okay, I'm excited now.
guides.note: Overlaps with guide 1 in warmth; differs in that relief at a resolved doubt is not required here — shared enthusiasm is.

guides.response_function: Registers the abrupt arrival and stays on what the email says
required_content: Treats the confirmation as landing suddenly rather than as expected all along
acceptable_variations: Asks what else the email says — dates, times, booking reference
Remarks on the timing of it arriving mid-conversation
must_avoid: Treating the gasp as distress and asking whether something went wrong
guides.example: That was fast — it literally just landed. What dates does it give?

guides.response_function: Registers the dates as wrong rather than treating news as good
required_content: Treats the confirmation as bad news about the dates, not the awaited relief
acceptable_variations: Asks what dates A actually booked or wanted
Suggests changing or checking with the airline/hotel
must_avoid: Congratulating A that the booking came through, or reading the groan as relief
guides.example: Oh no, that's not the week you wanted at all.

guides.response_function: Commiserates that the confirmation made trouble instead of settling it
required_content: Treats the long-awaited email as having created a hassle rather than closed the matter
acceptable_variations: Offers to help sort it out or make the call
Grumbles about how long it took to arrive for this
must_avoid: Framing the email's arrival as the problem being resolved
guides.example: Of course it shows up and now it's a whole thing to fix.

guides.response_function: Takes up the shortness of notice as the trouble
required_content: Treats how soon the trip falls as the problem, not the booking itself
acceptable_variations: Points out there's still time to pack or prepare
Notes A's week was open anyway, so it could work
must_avoid: Treating A as pleased the trip is imminent, or as objecting to the destination
guides.example: Next week? That's basically no time to get ready.
guides.note: Distinct from 1 in that the dates are the booked ones — the problem is their nearness, not an error.
